kinds.about: Mods: one folder per 16-digit title id, inside it one folder per mod holding exefs/, romfs/ or cheats/ (deeper folders work too), or the container files romfs.bin and exefs.nsp beside them, as Ryujinx's mods/contents/<title id>/<mod>.
kinds.doc: Ryujinx 1.3.3 (e2143d43) finds contents/<x16> case-insensitively and takes the first match (ModLoader.cs:160-161, 300-312), so an existing title folder in state is reused rather than doubled; it takes every child folder as a mod, descending until romfs, exefs or cheats (:163-201), and romfs.bin and exefs.nsp beside them (:278-294); a mod missing from games/<tid>/mods.json is enabled (:173-185, 263-275). It creates contents/<tid> only when absent (:204-213) and writes inside a mod only from the mod manager and cheat window, which a fullscreen launch never opens, so each mod folder and container file is linked inside a real title folder.

mods.doc: The library is <paths.mods>/ryujinx/contents/<title id>/<mod>; no setting is needed, a mod Ryujinx finds is on.

updates.about: Updates beside the ROMs in switch/updates, named like the owner's [0100F2C0115B6800][v393216].nsp: the highest version of each title is the one Ryujinx boots, the version saves and mods were made on.
updates.doc: Ryujinx 1.3.3 boots the update games/<base id x16>/updates.json selects (NcaExtensions.cs:144-163), a snake_case {selected, paths} (TitleUpdateMetadata.cs, JsonHelper.cs:21-28), and only for a patch of that base title ((id & ~0x1FFF) == base, :154-157): an update id is the base id plus 0x800. Its own update window writes the file (TitleUpdatesHelper.cs:54-77), never opened in a fullscreen launch; autoload runs only on a game-list reload (MainWindow.axaml.cs:707-720). Without it Semu's Ryujinx booted 1.0.0 of Tears of the Kingdom, whose save and mod are on v393216.

doc.package: Linux executes only the bundled source-built ${asset_root}/bin/Ryujinx. There is no Flatpak, host binary, or prebuilt Linux fallback.
doc.fullscreen: The pinned desktop parser consumes --fullscreen before the final ROM argument. Both platforms pass --graphics-backend vulkan.
doc.input: The managed Config.json contains the active Player1 GamepadSDL2 binding for the target Steam virtual controller. Ryujinx has no native save-state contract; app.quit remains process-group owned.
doc.keys: prod.keys and title.keys are copied into the isolated root-data system directory from read-only external/project sources without modifying those sources.
doc.saves: Native Switch game saves are emulator-owned at ${state_root}/config/Ryujinx/bis/user/save. Profile convergence owns only Config.json, so save data and installed firmware remain untouched.
doc.rendering: Vulkan on both platforms. render_vulkan composes Semu's bezel and shader into the swapchain image at present: on Linux through VK_LAYER_SEMU_compositor, on macOS through Semu's stand-in placed as Ryujinx's own libMoltenVK.dylib (packaging/nix/ryujinx_semu.nix).
doc.content: What Ryujinx 1.3.3 (e2143d43, narHash checked against the Nix store copy) loads: .xci, .nca, .nsp and .pfs0 (src/Ryujinx/Systems/AppHost.cs:819-846), anything else as homebrew, which is .nro or else NSO (859, src/Ryujinx.HLE/Loaders/Processes/ProcessLoader.cs:175-237). No archive: a .zip fails as unsupported homebrew.

menu.doc: Ryujinx declares no pause action, so the Semu menu draws over the running game; on Linux it holds the pad while it is open, so the game sees none of the menu's input.
